# Model specification: i2c-controller 1.0.0

Master-mode I2C controller as used by PX4 and ArduPilot for magnetometers, barometers and EEPROMs (7-bit addresses, automatic transfer length).

## Features

| Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|
| base | 7-bit master transfers with automatic length, repeated START, STOP and NACK. |
| dma | DMA requests. |

## Terms

| Term | Kind | Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| enable | control | base | The controller takes part in transfers. |
| target_address | control | base | 7-bit address of the child for the next transfer. |
| direction | control | base | Write (controller to child) or read (child to controller). |
| byte_count | control | base | Number of data bytes in the transfer (up to the IP limit per chunk). |
| auto_end | control | base | Send STOP automatically after byte_count bytes; otherwise wait for the driver (repeated START or STOP). |
| reload | control | base | More than byte_count bytes follow; a new byte_count is programmed when the chunk ends. |
| start | control | base | Begins the transfer with START and the address phase. |
| stop | control | base | Sends STOP after the current byte. |
| tx_data | data | base | Next byte to send. |
| rx_data | data | base | Last received byte. |
| tx_space | status | base | tx_data can take the next byte. |
| rx_available | status | base | A received byte can be read. |
| transfer_complete | status | base | byte_count bytes done, auto_end off, reload off: the driver must START again or STOP. |
| reload_complete | status | base | byte_count bytes done with reload on. |
| stop_detected | status | base | A STOP has ended the transaction. |
| nack | status | base | The child did not acknowledge the address or a byte. |
| busy | status | base | The bus is between START and STOP. |
| status_ack | ack | base | Clears stop_detected and nack. |
| irq_enables | control | base | Per-status interrupt enables (tx_space, rx_available, transfer_complete, stop_detected, nack, errors). |
| irq | event | base | Event interrupt line (and error line where the IP has two; Devicetree interrupts). |
| tx_dma_enable | control | dma | tx_space raises the transmit DMA request. |
| rx_dma_enable | control | dma | rx_available raises the receive DMA request. |
| tx_dma_request | event | dma | dmas entry tx. |
| rx_dma_request | event | dma | dmas entry rx. |

## Behaviour rules

| Rule | Feature | Rule text |
|---|---|---|
| ADV-I2C-B001 | base | start with enable on sends START and the address of target_address with direction; the child at that address acknowledges (ADV-I2C-003); with no child there, nack turns on and STOP follows. |
| ADV-I2C-B002 | base | In a write, each byte placed in tx_data while tx_space is on is sent once, in order, to the addressed child; a byte the child does not acknowledge sets nack and ends the transfer with STOP (ADV-I2C-004). |
| ADV-I2C-B003 | base | In a read, each byte from the child becomes readable at rx_data with rx_available on; the controller acknowledges all but the last byte of byte_count (ADV-I2C-005). |
| ADV-I2C-B004 | base | After byte_count bytes, with auto_end STOP is sent and stop_detected turns on; without auto_end and without reload transfer_complete turns on and the bus stays busy; with reload reload_complete turns on and a new byte_count continues the transfer. |
| ADV-I2C-B005 | base | start while transfer_complete is on gives a repeated START without STOP (ADV-I2C-006); stop ends the transaction, busy turns off and stop_detected turns on. |
| ADV-I2C-B006 | base | irq is raised while any status is on whose enable in irq_enables is on. |
| ADV-I2C-B007 | dma | rx_dma_request while rx_dma_enable and rx_available; tx_dma_request while tx_dma_enable and tx_space. |
| ADV-I2C-B008 | base | Each byte, address phase, START and STOP takes the bus time given by the timing register's clock; events are reported at those clocks. |

**Timing.** Byte and condition times follow the IP's timing register at the kernel clock; the timing rules of docs/device-tree-design.md apply.

**Out of scope.** slave mode, 10-bit addressing, SMBus (PEC, alert, timeouts), clock stretching by the child, multi-master arbitration loss, analog/digital filters (stored only)
